title: Nine Strokes of Ink
subtitle: 书法与手工艺 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 书法与手工艺（文学艺术与体育·手工艺与创造）
meta: 主题语境：书法与手工艺（文学艺术与体育·手工艺与创造）　|　核心词汇：calligraphy　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 calligraphy 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my mother was sent to copy ① calligraphy she could not read, and she said the reading was the whole of the lesson. The ② calligraphy, meaning the strokes and not the poem, was nine characters long and was copied by whoever came last; calligraphy, she said, is the only thing in a study that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ calligraphy in that album had the same seal, and the ④ calligraphy at the front, meaning the one the master wrote and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever copied properly. Calligraphy, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ calligraphy was the whole of the poem, meaning the verse it carried and not the strokes. The ⑥ calligraphy, meaning the poem and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody hangs and nobody questions; calligraphy, he said, is either something you copy or the only word that means both strokes and a poem. She said the poem is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ calligraphy had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the seal. The ⑧ calligraphy of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine strokes and eleven years of copying; calligraphy, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ calligraphy I remember is the one at the front, which was framed in 1976 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ piece of calligraphy, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being copied; every calligraphy, she said, is a poem that has agreed to look like strokes. She said the poem was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 书法；书法作品
B. n. 书法（指那些笔画本身，与诗相对）
C. 固定搭配：copy calligraphy 临摹书法
D. n. 书法（指册子里每一幅）
E. n. 书法（指前面那一幅）
F. n. 书法（抽象：它所承载的那首诗）
G. n. 那首诗（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The calligraphy, meaning the strokes and not the poem
calligraphy was the whole of the poem
the calligraphy had become a photograph in a report
The calligraphy of the whole thing
A piece of calligraphy, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: copy calligraphy 意为“临摹书法”，1955 年母亲被派去临摹一幅她读不懂的书法。
calligraphy 意为“书法”，指那些笔画本身而不是诗，共九个字，由最后走的人临摹。
calligraphy 指册子里每一幅书法，每一幅都是同样的印章。
calligraphy 指前面那一幅（老师写的那一幅），是唯一有人认真临摹过的。
calligraphy 意为“书法”，抽象指它所承载的那首诗，父亲说 calligraphy 就是那首诗的全部。
calligraphy 为抽象用法，指那首诗本身，是屋子里人人都挂、却没人质疑的东西。
calligraphy 意为“书法、书法作品”，到 1971 年这幅 calligraphy 成了报告里的一张照片。
calligraphy 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九笔和十一年的临摹。
calligraphy 意为“书法”，我记得的是前面那一幅，1976 年装裱，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
calligraphy 为抽象总称，祖母说一幅书法是唯一会因为被临摹而变好的东西。
